modules.intent: Workflow engine argv entrypoint. Keeps the top-level module thin so the CLI and application core stay in their own modules and `aver context` has a stable root to resume from.
Plain argv parsing for the workflow engine CLI. The parser stays shell-friendly and returns small typed inputs so the CLI adapter does not need to know any command semantics.

functions.desc: Parses argv-style input into a command, query, or help action.

modules.intent: Effectful command handlers for workflow mutations. The app layer is intentionally small: it decides a plan from persisted state, derives follow-up rule effects as data, then commits and dispatches that plan.
Shared domain types for the workflow engine. Keeps records and enums in one place so command, rule, and store modules can speak about the same application core without repeating shapes.
Pure project creation, lookup, and update helpers. Projects stay deliberately shallow: the task engine is event-sourced, but project lifecycle is simple enough to keep as direct state.

functions.desc: Linear lookup is sufficient for this intentionally small application core.
Replaces an existing project by ID or appends a new one.

modules.intent: Pure validation rules for command inputs and state transitions. Keeps task and project invariants inspectable without touching the store or clock.

functions.desc: Tags use the same restricted shape as IDs.

functions.desc: Checks fields needed to create a project.
verify: validateProjectCreate("alpha", "   ") -> Result.Err("Project name cannot be blank")
validateProjectCreate("bad id", "Alpha") -> Result.Err("Project ID must use letters, numbers, dash, or underscore")

modules.intent: Pure timestamp parsing and comparison for workflow deadlines and rule windows. Uses explicit ISO parsing instead of assuming Time.now() strings can only be compared lexicographically when duration math is needed.

functions.desc: Parses YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS and ignores any trailing fractional or zone suffix.
verify: parseIso("bad") -> Result.Err("Timestamp must start with YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS")
parseIso("2026-03-08T12:30:00Z") -> Result.Ok(Timestamp(year = 2026, month = 3, day = 8, hour = 12, minute = 30, second = 0))

functions.sig: withinNextHours(now: String, target: String, hours: Int) -> Result<Bool, String>
functions.desc: True when target is in the future and inside the requested hour window.

modules.intent: Pure task command logic that produces explicit events. Command handlers stay thin because this module converts validated user intent into domain events without touching persistence or notifications.

Pure event application and replay logic for workflow tasks. With typed sum payload matching now working across the toolchain, replay can live in the domain again instead of reconstructing state from serialized event fields.

functions.desc: True when the flat event log contains at least one event for the given task.
Linear lookup for replayed tasks.

modules.intent: Explicit workflow rule functions over replayed task state. Rules stay as plain functions rather than a hidden mini-language so reviewers can see which business pressure caused each follow-up event or notification.
Pure derived views and summaries over replayed task state. Deadlines, stalled work, and review-needed markers stay derived here instead of being hidden as imperative mutations.

functions.sig: deriveView(task: Task, now: String) -> Result<TaskView, String>
functions.desc: Builds derived flags without mutating stored priority or tags.

modules.intent: Flat-file persistence for projects and append-only task events. This module owns file formats and append/write primitives; replay stays in the domain so the app core reads like event sourcing instead of storage magic.

functions.desc: Base directory for workflow engine files.

modules.intent: Shared flat-file codec helpers for the workflow engine infra modules. The storage format is intentionally plain text, so escaping, optional fields, and line splitting stay explicit instead of being hidden in a serializer.

functions.desc: Escapes percent, pipe, and newline for one flat-file field.
Parses one stored boolean field.

functions.sig: fieldAt(parts: List<String>, index: Int, label: String) -> Result<String, String>
functions.desc: Reads and unescapes one required field from a split line.

modules.intent: Thin time adapter for the workflow engine. Keeping Time.now behind one module makes orchestration explicit about where time enters the system without contaminating pure domain logic.
Notification delivery and persistence for workflow rules. Notifications are stored so queries can inspect them later, but they are also emitted immediately to the console to make the CLI feel alive.

functions.desc: Reads all persisted notifications.
Persists and prints only new notifications.

modules.intent: Audit trail persistence for workflow actions and rule follow-ups. Audit entries stay outside the task event log because some audit records explain why a decision happened rather than representing state reconstruction inputs.

functions.desc: Reads all persisted audit entries.

modules.intent: Effectful read-model assembly for the workflow engine CLI. Queries load persisted state, replay tasks, and derive views without mixing those concerns into the parser or the pure domain modules.

Shell-friendly rendering for workflow engine command and query results. Formatting stays dumb and explicit so the interesting orchestration remains in the app and domain layers, not in presentation glue.

functions.desc: Maps command execution into rendered output.
Maps query execution into rendered output.

decisions.name: OneRulePassPerCommand
decisions.reason: Workflow rules should stay reviewable, not turn into an implicit fixpoint engine. A single pass after each user mutation keeps command flow explicit even if it leaves some second-order derivations for a later manual `run_rules` call.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: ProjectsStayStateBased
decisions.reason: Project transitions are shallow compared with task lifecycle. A separate project event log would add ceremony without revealing new pressure. Keeping projects as direct state lets the task event stream stay focused on richer behavior.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: ArchivedProjectsRejectTaskChanges
decisions.reason: Archived projects are an operational boundary, not only a display state. Once a project is archived, task mutation should stop unless a future command makes that exception explicit.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: CommandsProduceEventsNotMutatedTasks
decisions.reason: A task workflow engine should make state transitions reviewable at the event level. Returning events instead of directly mutated tasks keeps replay and audit aligned.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: ReplayReturnsToDomain
decisions.reason: Replay belongs with the domain semantics, not inside the storage adapter. Now that constructor payload matching is reliable enough, the natural typed version is clearer than the old serialized-payload workaround.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: RulesStayAsFunctions
decisions.reason: The rule count is small enough that a DSL would mostly hide branching. Explicit functions keep rule-specific edge cases near the code they affect.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: DeadlinesProjectUrgencyInsteadOfMutatingPriority
decisions.reason: Stored priority represents intent; deadline pressure is situational. Mutating priority during rule evaluation would erase who set the original priority.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: AppendOnlyTaskEventsWithFlatProjectState
decisions.reason: Task lifecycle is where reviewable history matters, so an append-only event log pays for itself. Projects are much shallower, and storing them as current state avoids a second event system. This keeps the storage model simple while still exercising replay in a realistic place.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: TimeEntersThroughClockModule
decisions.reason: Deadline and stalled rules depend on the current time, but that dependency should remain visible at the app boundary instead of leaking into pure domain modules.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: NotificationsDeduplicateByKey
decisions.reason: Deadline and overdue rules can be re-run manually, so delivery needs a stable idempotency key or the CLI will drown in repeated warnings.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: AuditsStayAdjacentToEventsNotInsideThem
decisions.reason: Reopen reasons and command traces are valuable to reviewers, but they should not change replay semantics for task state.
decisions.author: Codex

decisions.name: QueriesReplayInsteadOfReadingMutableTaskTables
decisions.reason: The whole point of the workflow engine is to see whether replay stays readable. If queries bypass replay with a separate mutable task table, that test becomes fake.
decisions.author: Codex
